statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 14% (low) after a third observed hour of the CME reopen, with NQZ26 at 31,148.25, up 0.28%, on 13,092 contracts inside a 22-point band and the last print at the top of it. Stress is 64% (elevated) as Iran keeps the Strait of Hormuz declared closed on seven conditions while Brent 102.53 and WTI 90.66 both ease, and the 10-year sits at 5.2939%, a more-than-two-decade high.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON and the published forecast path holds EA_ON across all 24 hours. The narrow danger window is drawn across the 13:00-15:00Z block on 5 October, 15:00-17:00 Berlin, covering the US cash open, the S&P Global services finals at 13:45Z and the September ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z, where the published Tail path peaks at 16% on scheduled-catalyst grounds rather than on observed one-way structure. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this state.
headline: Tail edges to 14% as a third thin reopen hour holds NQZ26 at the top of a 22-point band, while easing crude against a declared Hormuz closure keeps Stress at 64%
body:
The CME equity-index reopen is now roughly two and a half hours old and it has produced an orderly, very thin bid rather than a price path worth protecting against. NQZ26 prints 31,148.25, up 86.50 points or 0.28% on a 31,061.75 prior close, with volume building from roughly 7,900 contracts an hour ago to 13,092 now. For the first time this session a range has actually printed: 31,126.00 to 31,148.25, a 22.25-point band worth about 0.07% of index value, with the last trade sitting at the high of it. Price holding the session extreme on building volume is the amplifier the contract names, but at this magnitude the band is noise rather than structure, and there is no retracement large enough to pass or fail.

Tail rises one point to 14%, which stays deep inside the low band and maps to EA_ON and green. The increase reflects a third consecutive observed hour of mild upward drift from a record Friday close, into an Asian tape that is missing mainland China and South Korea for holidays, so depth is unusually shallow and an unopposed extension is the realistic channel if one appears. What the increase deliberately does not reflect is event importance or headline severity. The single most informative piece of cross-asset evidence tonight is that Iran's parliament speaker hardened the Strait of Hormuz closure to seven conditions on 4 October and a fourth tanker of the month was struck by an unknown projectile, with crew safe, and crude went down anyway. Brent is 102.53, off 0.18%, against a 105.28 settle on 28 September; WTI is 90.66, off 0.49%. Aggregated reporting on Gulf flow recovery is genuinely conflicting, with one strand describing traffic at a small fraction of pre-war levels and another describing flows near 98% of them, so the published assessment leans on the verified price rather than on either figure.

The standing constraint on this index is rates, not geopolitics. Friday's September payroll report missed badly at 29,000 against an 84,000 consensus, with July revised to a loss of 10,000 and August cut to 133,000, and unemployment up to 4.2%. Yields fell on the print and then reversed higher, closing above Thursday's levels: the 10-year at 5.2939%, up 5.99 basis points and at its highest in more than two decades, the 2-year at 4.8414%, with the Federal Reserve H.15 release showing 5.24% and 4.78% as of 1 October and the 30-year at 5.61%. The Nasdaq-100 still closed at a record 30,807.93, up 1.00%, and VIX fell 6.59% to 15.31. That combination is what holds Stress at 64%, the top of the elevated band, while Tail sits at 14%: a difficult, expensive environment that has so far kept mean-reverting, not a pathological path.

Confidence is 85%, a point lower than the previous hour. The evidence base is strong on the things that matter most, with verified futures levels and volume, real-time Brent and WTI, H.15 yields, the complete payroll actuals and revisions, and the week's US calendar. Two deductions apply: the Hormuz flow reporting is internally contradictory, and the shared Finviz context file carries a 29 September collection time, roughly six days stale against the 90-minute freshness contract, so it was treated as unavailable and no breadth, megacap or semiconductor cross-check was folded in. VIX is also a Friday cash close rather than a live read. The dominant mode stays normal: a 0.07% overnight band is not a trend.

The published path holds Tail at 14% through the Tokyo handoff, where a thin book remains the main channel for unopposed extension, then decays to a 12% to 13% range once Asian and European depth is expected to establish two-way trade. It ticks to 13% for the 07:00Z European cash open as a liquidity-transition allowance, returns to 12% through the European morning, and rises into the US session: 15% for the 13:00Z hour containing the cash open and the S&P Global finals, and a 16% session peak for the 14:00Z hour containing September ISM Services, whose employment component carries extra weight after a 29,000 payroll gain. Both increases are scheduled-catalyst allowances, not assertions that opening continuation has already been observed. The path then decays through the afternoon, ticks to 14% for the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close given the record-close starting point and closing-imbalance flow, and settles at 12% across the maintenance break and the overnight handoff into 6 October. Every published hour stays in the low band and maps to EA_ON.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours are available from Claude history. Tail was held at 3% from 00:00Z through 21:00Z on 4 October, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout with the dominant mode normal, because the CME equity-index complex was halted for the weekend and no Nasdaq-100 price path was scoreable. Tail then rose to 12% in the 22:00Z slot once the reopen had been observed and to 13% at 23:00Z as the drift extended. Stress climbed from 72% at 00:00Z to a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on the accumulating weekend Hormuz and Gulf incident flow, then eased steadily through the 73%, 70%, 68%, 66% and 64% readings into the 14:00Z trough as the headlines failed to transmit into crude, drifted back to 71% by 21:00Z, and settled at 66% and 65% across the two reopen hours. Confidence ran a narrow 83% to 88% band, peaking in the European and early US hours when verified evidence was densest and easing into the thin weekend and reopen hours.
outlookSummary: The current hour contains a third observed hour of the reopen, which has extended the gap to 0.28% on 13,092 contracts and printed a first 22-point range with the last trade at its high, so Tail edges to 14% while Stress eases to 64% on softer crude and an unchanged 15.31 VIX. Tail holds 14% through the Tokyo handoff, where a book missing mainland China and South Korea remains the main channel for unopposed extension, then decays to a 12% to 13% range once Asian and European depth is expected to establish two-way trade. It ticks to 13% for the 07:00Z European cash open as a liquidity-transition allowance, returns to 12% through the European morning, and rises to 15% and a 16% session peak across the 13:00Z and 14:00Z hours carrying the US cash open, the S&P Global services finals and September ISM Services. Those increases are scheduled-catalyst allowances rather than observed structure. The path decays through the US afternoon, ticks to 14% for the power hour into the 20:00Z cash close given the record-close starting point, and settles at 12% across the maintenance break and the overnight handoff into 6 October. Every published hour remains in the low band and maps to EA_ON, with Stress tracking a 61% to 68% range and Confidence a 80% to 85% range.

forecastDetail.comment: Third observed hour of the CME reopen: NQZ26 31,148.25, up 0.28% on 13,092 contracts inside a 22-point band, with the last print at the top of it. Volume has roughly doubled from the prior hour while the range stayed inside 0.1%, so the drift is thin rather than structural. Brent 102.53 and WTI 90.66 are both easing despite Iran's declared Hormuz closure, which is the clearest cross-asset evidence that the weekend geopolitical headlines are not transmitting. The conditional risk is an unopposed extension of the reopen drift in a shallow book rather than anything observed; a rotation back under 31,126.00 would restore two-way trade and invalidate it. The assumption behind these scores is that two-way trade persists and no fresh Gulf shipping incident transmits into crude; the fourth reported tanker strike of the month on 4 October is the standing reminder that this assumption can break between assessments.

Late Asian trade. The conditional Tail path decays to 12% as reopen hours accumulate without producing a scoreable one-way leg. Confidence eases to 82% because the live price-path evidence anchoring the score is ageing and no verified observation exists for this hour.
